summary: South Dakota's sitting governor, Larry Rhoden (Republican), who took office in 2025, ran for a full term and won, defeating Dan Ahlers (Democrat).

candidates.name: Larry Rhoden
candidates.bio: Larry Rhoden became governor of South Dakota in January 2025 after Kristi Noem resigned. He previously served as lieutenant governor and in the state legislature, and is a rancher.

positions.summary: Signed property tax cuts that his office calls the largest in South Dakota history, paid for partly with reserve funds and a scheduled return of the state sales tax from 4.2% to 4.5%.
Says supporting rural health care is a top priority.
Points to the "Data Center Bill of Rights" as putting guardrails on data centers.
Pointed to recent legislation making it a felony to advertise, distribute or sell abortion pills.

candidates.name: Dan Ahlers
candidates.bio: Dan Ahlers is a former South Dakota state senator who served as Senate Democratic leader. He was the Democratic nominee for governor in 2026.

positions.summary: Opposes a state income tax, saying South Dakota's budget surpluses make one unnecessary, and says cost of living is a top concern.
Says he would keep rural hospitals and long-term care facilities open, address health care workforce shortages and expand mental health services.
Says he would recruit and retain teachers, strengthen rural schools, expand early childhood education and childcare access, and create afterschool programs.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called)
